analysis_steps.goal: Parametric visibility modelling of the ALMA Band 6 continuum emission

method.value: Compute dust temperatures and 1.3 mm model images with RADMC-3D for two radial surface density parameterisations (power-law 'SPL' with 9 free parameters and Gaussian 'SGR' with 8 free parameters), transform to model visibilities at the observed uv-baselines, and fit using MCMC with emcee.

evidence.quote: We modelled the system with two belt distributions, ‘model SPL’, defined by an inner edge ($r_1$), outer edge ($r_2$), and power-law profile, with an index ($p_{\rm{SPL}}$) for a total of 9 free parameters, and ‘model SGR’, defined by a peak emission radius ($r_1$) and Gaussian width ($\sigma_{\rm{SGR}}$; the standard deviation of the Gaussian distribution) for a total of 8 free parameters.
We used the *RADMC-3D* package (cite: Dullemond12) with the mcmc parameter estimator, $\it{emcee}$ (cite: Goodman10; FM13) to compute the dust temperature of our disc models.
These dust temperatures were used to create 2D images at $1.3\,$mm and subsequently used to compute model visibilities at identical uv-baselines to our ALMA observations.

key_parameters.value: Free parameters: M_dust, r_1, i, PA, F_*_B6, x_off, y_off, plus (p_SPL, r_2) for SPL or (sigma_SGR) for SGR; N_Dat = 12,104,328

For our Band 6 data, there are $2\times N_{\rm{Vis}} = N_{\rm{Dat}}=12,104,328$ independent data points, accounting for the real and imaginary components of the interferometric visibilities.

analysis_steps.goal: Grid modelling of the HST scattered light emission

method.value: Generate a grid of 0.6 um scattered light models based on the SPL power-law geometry using Henyey-Greenstein phase functions (and Mie theory test), apply a null map mask, scale by a dummy flux pre-factor, and minimise reduced chi^2 against the HST image.

evidence.quote: In this investigation, we fixed the inner and outer edges of the disc to 73 au and 280 au respectively (based on the peak brightness of the HST observations, and the outer edge at which scattered light emission was observed in $\S$3.2), the position angle to 148$^{\circ}$, and produced a suite of models, based on variations of the disc inclination (ranging from 25 to 60$^\circ$ in 5$^\circ$ increments), scattering factors (ranging from 0.1 to 0.9 in 0.1 increments) and power-law indices (ranging from -2 to 2 in 0.5 increments).

A noise estimate from the raw data was obtained from emission unaffected by real scattered light emission, i.e., beyond 280 au, with which the reduced $\chi^2$, $\chi^2_\nu$, of each residual image (HST data minus model) could then be measured.

key_parameters.value: r_in = 73 au, r_out = 280 au, PA = 148 deg; grid over i = 25 to 60 deg (step 5 deg), g = 0.1 to 0.9 (step 0.1), gamma = -2 to 2 (step 0.5)

assumptions.value: Henyey-Greenstein scattering phase function (also tested spherical grains with Mie theory)

evidence.quote: set up to produce images of scattered light emission at 0.6 $\mu$m, with a range of anisotropic scattering factors ($g$) based on the Henyey-Greenstein (HG) scattering function (cite: HG41).

fitting.value: Grid search minimising reduced chi^2 with a free flux scaling pre-factor.

evidence.quote: To find the best-fit of the model suite, we introduced a dummy pre-factor which each model was multiplied by before the data was subtracted (used to scale the emission brightness to maximise the goodness-of-fit, which was also varied in order to minimise the $\chi^2$ of each model).
